slot.brief: Combustion/limiting-reagent problem mixing gas volumes and mole counts; find leftover reactant or product moles, difficulty via impure sample or back-titration style bookkeeping.

stem: A $10.0$ g impure sample containing $80.0\%$ $\text{CaC}_2$ reacts with excess water. The acetylene formed is ignited with $5.60$ L of $\text{O}_2$ at STP. How many moles of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ remain after cooling? Take $M(\text{CaC}_2)=64$ g mol$^{-1}$ and the molar volume at STP as $22.4$ L mol$^{-1}$. Impurities are inert.

verdicts.working: CaC₂ = 8.00/64 = 0.125 mol, so 0.125 mol C₂H₂ forms. O₂ = 5.60/22.4 = 0.250 mol; at 2.5 mol O₂ per mol C₂H₂, this burns 0.100 mol C₂H₂. Remaining = 0.0250 mol.

working:
$n_{\text{CaC}_2}=\dfrac{10.0(0.800)}{64}=0.125$ mol; $n_{\text{C}_2\text{H}_2}=0.125$ mol
$n_{\text{O}_2}=\dfrac{5.60}{22.4}=0.250$ mol
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_2+\dfrac{5}{2}\text{O}_2\to2\text{CO}_2+\text{H}_2\text{O}$
$n_{\text{C}_2\text{H}_2,\,reacted}=\dfrac{0.250}{5/2}=0.100$ mol
$n_{\text{left}}=0.125-0.100=0.0250$ mol

Independent check: CaC₂ = 8.00/64 = 0.125 mol, so 0.125 mol C₂H₂ forms. O₂ = 5.60/22.4 = 0.250 mol; at 2.5 mol O₂ per mol C₂H₂, this burns 0.100 mol C₂H₂. Remaining = 0.0250 mol.
